Hi Samira — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, and we'll attach evidence:

1) RTO / RPO by tier:
   - Hosted (standard): RTO target 15 minutes for control-plane failover, RPO <= 5 minutes for model state (KV cache best-effort; persistent data replicated every 1 minute).
   - Hosted (premium SLA): RTO target 5 minutes, RPO <= 1 minute with cross-region replication enabled.
   - Dedicated: Customer-configurable, default template 10 min RTO / 1 min RPO with reserved capacity failover policy.
   - Embeddings/batch: We treat long-running jobs with checkpointing; roll-forward approach keeps RPO to last successful checkpoint (typically < 2 minutes for jobs with periodic commits).

2) Multi-region failover:
   - Default: automated health-based routing + canary cutover; automated fallback to regional standby when primary fails healthchecks for 45s.
   - DNS: low TTL (60s) for API gateway entries, plus global anycast + regional edge routing to reduce DNS propagation reliance.
   - Session continuity: ephemeral KV caches are rebuilt via warm-up and prefix caching; for strict session affinity we advise token-based sticky routing (session token tied to region) — seamless continuity depends on model context size and KV cache rehydration time.

3) Evidence: attaching runbook summary and latest full-region failover results (2026-09-30). The CSV includes timeline markers and operator actions. Post-mortem summary attached.

4) KMS/HSM: We integrate with customer KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM) via a key-wrapping model. Keys are not replicated between regions; instead we rewrap using a secondary key in the target region during failover. For HSM-backed keys we support re-keying workflows with pre-approved key material; we note this in the runbook as a manual step if customer policy requires HSM-bound keys that cannot be exported.

I'll coordinate a 45-minute Q&A next week; suggested times: Wed 12/9 10:00 PT or Thu 12/10 13:00 PT. Ben, Laura — looping you in for any additional technical specifics.

Thanks,

Team — drafting consolidated responses to Kensington's follow-ups. Key items to confirm before I send:

1) Premium SLA coverage: confirm list of covered failure modes and standard exclusions. Suggest: covered = single AZ failure, regional resource exhaustion (computed at infra layer), most cloud provider control-plane transient errors when they affect instance management; excluded = provider-wide outage where network backbone is severed from region to edge, customer-side network/firewall misconfigurations, and deliberate operator-initiated maintenance windows with prior notice.

2) KV cache warm-up worst-case: with our current prefetch + parallel streaming warm-up we see 30–90s depending on model size. For 2k token sessions + 50k prefix entries, worst-case cold rebuild ~ 120s (we should give worst-case 2 minutes). Attach kv-cache-warmup-snippet.txt for the algorithm notes.

3) Audit trail: we will sanitize the 2026-09-30 failover CSV and produce an events timeline PDF with operator ids masked; confirm PII masking is acceptable.

Any objections? Ben — commercial impact if we promise 5-minute RTO for region-wide provider control-plane issues? I think we should restrict that in the exclusion list.

-Mateo
